STEP 1 - Vessel type: Flat square plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall, and no shadowed interior.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a square plate is typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium, near the small end.
b) Reference: the sprouts are about 3.5 cm across. The plate spans about 365 px and a sprout about 60 px, so 365/60 × 3.5 ≈ 21 cm.
Both cues agree on about 22 cm square.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Brussels sprouts (roasted, charred, with oil). Counting the visible sprouts gives 13. They form a single layer with little stacking, so there are essentially no hidden pieces. A medium cooked sprout weighs about 19-20 g, so 13 × 19 ≈ 250 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No base layer (no rice, sauce, or greens) is visible under the sprouts. The plate is sparsely covered, so no additional items are added.

STEP 5 - Energy: Roasted Brussels sprouts with oil are about 60 kcal per 100 g as served.
250 g × 0.60 kcal/g ≈ 150 kcal.
